column3: Donut chart that splits non-local datastores by their storage type property, with one slice per type found. Datastores flagged as local are left out.
Donut chart showing how many ESXi hosts run each distinct BIOS version, with one slice per version string found.
Donut chart grouping ESXi hosts by their reported BIOS version, one slice per version. Useful for spotting hosts that lag the firmware standard.

Per-host table of ESXi version and build, BIOS, CPU sockets, cores, model and speed, memory, datastore and NIC counts, hyperthreading, power policy, vMotion, shell and SSH state, and active storage paths. Ends with an average row.

Wide per-host inventory table covering hardware vendor and model, ESXi and BIOS versions, CPU, memory, NTP and SNMP and SSH service state, storage paths, NICs, port group security rollups, parent cluster, datacenter and vCenter, and serial and service tags.
Bar chart counting ESXi hosts by physical core count, using fixed buckets that run from 0 to 100 cores and a final open-ended bucket for larger hosts.
Bar chart counting ESXi hosts by total CPU capacity in GHz, in fixed buckets that step from 0 up to 300 GHz and beyond.
Donut chart showing how many ESXi hosts have each physical CPU socket count, one slice per distinct value.
Donut chart showing the share of ESXi hosts by hardware vendor model, one slice per model string.
Bar chart counting ESXi hosts by installed physical memory, in fixed buckets of a quarter terabyte up to more than 2 TB.
Donut chart showing how many ESXi hosts report each network link speed, one slice per distinct speed value.
Donut chart showing how many ESXi hosts have each number of active storage paths, one slice per distinct count.
Donut chart of ESXi hosts grouped by their full version and build string, one slice per version found in the environment.
Donut chart showing the share of ESXi hosts by hardware vendor, one slice per vendor name.
Donut chart showing how many ESXi hosts are capable of hyperthreading and how many are not.
Pie chart splitting ESXi hosts by whether the NTP daemon service is running.
Lists ESXi hosts whose maintenance state is in maintenance, with connection state, power state, powered-on flag, hardware model and parent cluster, ordered by cluster.

Table for distributed virtual switches with per-host check results for configuration sync, teaming mismatch, MTU mismatch, unsupported MTU and unsupported VLAN. Its host columns are bound to one specific host instance.

Lists ESXi hosts that are powered off, not connected, unavailable, in maintenance or in quarantine, with their power, connection, maintenance and quarantine states, version and cluster. A host matching any one condition appears.

Per-host table over the last day of core and thread CPU utilization, memory consumed and demand, ballooned, compressed and swapped memory, VM co-stop and ready percentages, and worst co-stop and ready values. Sorted by core utilization, highest first.
Donut chart showing how many ESXi hosts have vMotion enabled and how many do not.
Line chart of the 20-second peak guest CPU queue length for virtual machines, covering the previous 90 days.
Donut chart showing how many virtual machines run each guest operating system name, one slice per name.
Donut chart of virtual machines grouped by the guest operating system name reported by VMware Tools, one slice per name.
Line chart of guest memory page-in and page-out rates for virtual machines over the last week.
Table of guest file system partitions for a virtual machine, showing capacity in GB, used space in GB and percent used. The columns are tied to the root partition.
Lists datastores flagged as local that hold at least one virtual machine, showing the VM count per datastore, highest first.
Table for management services components with a 15-minute availability value and the peak and average memory utilization against requests.
Lists platform nodes of the management services with maximum CPU usage, memory usage, disk usage and status, each ordered highest first.
Lists platform volumes of the management services with their volume group, component name and volume utilization percent, highest utilization first.

Per-VM configuration table with guest hostname, hardware version, guest OS as set in vCenter and as reported by Tools, vCPU and socket counts, memory, NIC count, missing guest counter flag, creation date, encryption state and snapshot consolidation need.
Pie chart of virtual machines that have a CPU limit above zero, grouped by the limit value.
Bar chart placing virtual machines in 2 percent-wide buckets of 99th percentile peak CPU ready over one week, from 0 to 10 percent and above, with buckets colored green to red.
Bar chart of powered-on virtual machines by peak CPU ready percentile over the last day, in four buckets that end with 16 percent and above.
Bar chart counting virtual machines by configured vCPU count, in buckets of 8 up to 32, then 48, 64 and larger.
Line chart of virtual machine CPU net run time and CPU usage percent over the previous week.
Bar chart placing virtual machines in six buckets by 99th percentile peak virtual disk latency over one week, from under 50 ms to above 1000 ms, colored green to red.
Bar chart placing virtual machines in four buckets by 99th percentile peak disk latency over one week: under 25 ms, 25 to 50, 50 to 100 and above 100 ms.
Donut chart of virtual machines that have a CPU reservation above zero, one slice per reservation value in GHz.
Donut chart showing how many virtual machines have each CPU shares-per-vCPU value, one slice per value.
Donut chart showing how many virtual machines are configured with each vCPU count, one slice per size.
Bar chart counting virtual machines by the number of vCPUs recommended for addition, in buckets of 1, 2 to 4, 4 to 8, 8 to 12 and more.
Bar chart of virtual machines whose provisioned disk space is above 500 GB, grouped in terabyte-scale buckets from under 0.25 TB to over 8 TB.
Donut chart of virtual machines with a memory reservation above zero, one slice per reservation value in GB.
Donut chart showing how many virtual machines have each memory shares-per-MB value, one slice per value.
Bar chart counting virtual machines by the amount of memory in GB recommended for addition, in buckets from 1 GB up to 32 GB and above.
Bar chart counting oversized virtual machines by how many vCPUs could be reclaimed, in buckets from 1 up to 16 and above.
Bar chart of powered-off virtual machines grouped by disk space used, in terabyte buckets from under 1 TB to over 20 TB.
Bar chart counting oversized virtual machines by how much memory in GB could be reclaimed, in buckets from 1 GB up to 32 GB and above.
Bar chart counting virtual machines by snapshot age in days, in buckets of up to 2, 2 to 7, 7 to 14 and over 14 days.
Bar chart showing how many virtual machines use each virtual hardware version, one bar per version.
Bar chart placing virtual machines in six buckets by 99th percentile peak memory contention over one week, from 0 to 10 percent and above, colored green to red.
Bar chart placing virtual machines in four buckets by 99th percentile peak memory contention over the last day: under 2, 2 to 4, 4 to 8 and above 8 percent.
Donut chart showing how many virtual machines are configured with each memory size in GB, one slice per size.
Pie chart of virtual machines that have a memory limit above zero. Its charted column reads the CPU limit value rather than a memory value, so the slices need checking before use.
Bar chart counting virtual machines by configured memory in GB, in doubling buckets from under 16 GB to above 512 GB.
Bar chart of idle virtual machines grouped by consumed memory in GB, in buckets of up to 32, 64, 128 and larger.
Per-VM table of network adapter details: IP address, MAC address, port group and adapter type for the first adapter instance.
Per-VM table of power state, NIC count, IP address, MAC address count, datacenter, cluster and guest operating system.

Lists virtual machines whose average network throughput exceeds 12 over the last week, with 20-second, 5-minute and 1-hour peak throughput in Gbit/s, peak packet rate, NIC count, IP address and datacenter.

Lists powered-on VMs over the last 12 hours with guest hostname, three KPI scores, peak CPU queue, CPU ready, memory contention, disk queue, disk latency and transmit packet drop, plus vCPU, memory and virtual disk counts. Worst KPI first.
Bar chart of virtual machines whose snapshot age is above one day, grouped by snapshot size in GB: under 100, 100 to 200, 200 to 400 and larger.
Bar chart counting virtual machines by total snapshot size in GB, in buckets of up to 50, 100, 250 and 500 GB and larger.
Lists virtual machines that use snapshot space, with snapshot name, age in days, size in GB and last access time. The columns point at a single snapshot instance.
Lists virtual machines whose average disk IOPS exceeds 10 over the last week, with peak IOPS and throughput at 5-minute and 1-hour granularity, plus datacenter. Highest 5-minute IOPS first.
Donut chart showing how many virtual machines are in each VMware Tools version status, one slice per status.
Pie chart of virtual machines that have more than one virtual disk, grouped by disk count.
Bar chart counting virtual machines by number of virtual disks, in buckets of five from 0 up to 30 and above.

Per-VM table of virtual disk details: label, size in GB, datastore, raw device mapping flag, IOPS limit, provisioning format, SCSI controller type and bus sharing. Columns are bound to the first disk instance.
Bar chart counting virtual machines that have CPU hot add set to true.
Bar chart counting virtual machines whose memory hot add setting is anything other than false.
Bar chart counting virtual machines that have CPU hot remove set to true.
Bar chart of virtual machines that have more than one network adapter, grouped by adapter count.
Bar chart counting running virtual machines that are not reporting guest memory counters.
Donut chart showing how many virtual machines run each VMware Tools version, one slice per version number.
Donut chart of clusters with HA admission control enabled, grouped by the admission control policy in use.

Per-cluster configuration table covering type, host and datastore counts, HA and admission control settings, DRS enablement, automation, affinity rules, migration and imbalance thresholds, plus profile and workload management flags. Has a totals row.
Bar chart counting clusters by reserved CPU capacity in GHz, in five equal buckets across the observed range.
Bar chart counting clusters by total number of virtual machines, in buckets of 250 up to 1000, then 2000 and above.
Donut chart showing how many clusters have DPM enabled and how many do not.
Donut chart of clusters grouped by their DRS migration threshold setting, one slice per value, sorted ascending.
Donut chart of clusters grouped by the default DRS VM behavior, such as manual or fully automated, one slice per value.
Donut chart showing how many clusters have DRS enabled and how many do not.
Donut chart showing how many clusters have HA admission control enabled, using a window from the previous 7 days to now.
Donut chart showing how many clusters have vSphere HA enabled and how many do not.
Bar chart counting clusters by reserved memory in TB, in five equal buckets across the observed range.

Top 20 clusters over the last day by performance score (current, minimum and percentile), with worst CPU ready, worst co-stop, VM memory contention, running VM count and vSAN flag. Lowest score first.
Top 20 clusters with running VMs over the last month: worst VM CPU ready and memory contention at the percentile, share of VMs affected by each, and average running VMs. Has an average row.
Bar chart showing how many clusters contain each number of ESXi hosts, one bar per host count.
Per-datacenter table of peak total, physical and virtual network throughput in Gbit/s, running VMs and running hosts, highest throughput first. Has an average row.
Inventory table showing, for each datacenter, the number of clusters, hosts, datastores and VMs, plus the parent vCenter. Sorted by clusters then hosts, highest first.
Table for distributed switches with host count, switch version, NIC teaming policy and the teaming and VLAN/MTU health check results.
Inventory table for distributed switches: used and maximum port counts, VM count, host count, folder and tag.
Line chart for ESXi hosts of provisioned, usable and consumed memory and memory demand in GB over the previous week.
Lists VMs by 99th percentile peak memory contention, disk latency and CPU ready over one week. Summary rows show the average and worst value across all VMs.

Wide table for distributed port groups with used and maximum ports, VM count, backing type, VLAN and trunk, override permissions, security policy settings, segment and switch IDs and uplink. Highest used ports first.
Inventory table for distributed port groups showing uplink, active uplinks, port count, VM count and used ports.
Bar chart counting distributed port groups where promiscuous mode is allowed.
Table of resource pool settings: CPU and memory limits, reservations, expandable flags and shares, running and total VM counts, and tag.
Resource pool table combining running VM count, CPU and memory contention, CPU usage, effective limit, and CPU and memory limits, reservations, shares and expandable flags.
Bar chart showing how many distributed switches run each switch version, one bar per version.
